documents.text: Each value in Rust has an owner. There can only be one owner at a time. When the owner goes out of scope, the value will be dropped.
At any given time, you can have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references. References must always be valid.
Cargo.toml describes dependencies in broad terms. Cargo.lock contains exact information about dependencies. Cargo.lock records the exact dependency versions used by a build.
The cargo test command runs tests. A Rust test is a function annotated with the test attribute. A test fails when its thread panics.

questions.text: What happens when an owner goes out of scope in Rust?
How many mutable references can exist at a given time?
Which Cargo file records exact dependency versions?
How are Rust values dropped and how does a Rust test fail?
answers: A value is dropped when its owner goes out of scope; a test fails when its thread panics.
